name: Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite
biography: Author (of uncertain but probably late fifth-century date, likely a disciple of Proclus) of an influential work reconciling Neoplatonism with Christianity, mistakenly believed in the Middle Ages to be Saint Paul's Athenian convert; John the Scot's translation of his work (860) transmitted Neoplatonic negative theology into Catholic philosophy.
